children: Adani Group has drawn up a strategy to reduce passenger user fees at its airports to bare minimum by scaling up non-aeronautical business and city side development, CEO of its Airports Business Arun Bansal said on Wednesday.

The Airports Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA) determines aeronautical tariffs at major airports including landing charges and user development fees. Under the current regulatory framework, 30 per cent of non-aeronautical income of airports is used to cross subsidise aeronautical tariff.

Bansal said last year, aeronautical charges contributed to 60 per cent of revenue at its eight airports while the remainder came from non-aeronautical sources such as retail, food and beverage, advertising etc. By 2030 the revenue profile of airports will change and 70 per cent of revenue will come from non-aeronautical sources, he said at the SBI Banking & Economics Conclave 2026.
Bansal remarked that the group’s ambition is to bring regulatory charges for passengers so low that they become irrelevant.

Earlier this month, Adani group raised $1 billion by selling 5.5 per cent stake in its airports business. Funds raised from share sale will be used for expansion of Navi Mumbai and other airports. The group has drawn up $10 billion capex plan to expand airports. This includes upgrades to the airport at Ahmedabad before Commonwealth Games in 2030 as well as facilities in Jaipur and Thiruvananthapuram.

Bansal said the aim is to keep infrastructure ready considering massive aircraft orders placed by Indian carriers. The West Asia crisis that highlighted India’s dependence on hubs like Dubai and Doha has also pushed government to fast track India’s ambitions to develop aviation hubs. Bansal said Navi Mumbai airport has potential and is being planned as a hub. He added that the group also wishes to have US immigration pre-clearance facilities at Navi Mumbai but the government will have to evaluate the request. “It has to be a government decision. If it agrees we will do necessary infrastructure works,” he said.
Navi Mumbai airport began handling freighter flights from August. All freighter flights from Mumbai are expected to shift to Navi Mumbai airport by October 15.
Navi Mumbai airport began handling freighter flights from August

Earlier this month, AERA modified its tariff order enabling Navi Mumbai airport to offer concessions in landing charges to airlines. The airport operator is also making modification to airport for easier transit connections.

The group also wants airlines to shift 30 per cent of their international flights from Mumbai to Navi Mumbai airport. This is being proposed as it plans to redevelop Terminal 1 at Mumbai in phases. However airlines are unwilling to move their existing flights to Navi Mumbai considering connectivity challenges and uncertain demand.

title: We want to reduce passenger user fees to bare minimum: Adani Airports CEO Arun Bansal
